open_points.subject: ExpenseAllocation amount validity and persistence
open_points.text: M29 permits persisted `amount: Decimal` “as instructed, M26”, and M26 says “zero and negative amounts are accepted”; the Modeling conventions say “Negative amounts never appear in stored records; negative values exist only in derived balances.”
open_points.question: May an ExpenseAllocation persist a negative amount, or must negative allocation instructions be rejected despite M26 and M29?
options: Accept and persist negative ExpenseAllocation amounts when the non-empty allocation set sums to the expense total.
Reject any negative allocation instruction because persisted records cannot contain negative amounts.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the specific changed rules in M26 and M29: accept and persist negative allocations when the allocation set satisfies the sum invariant.

witness.initial: An active project has a section, and an operator submits a confirmed EUR expense with total_amount 100.
events: The authenticated operator supplies two allocation instructions: -10 to the section and 110 to other_expenses.
The expense-intake action validates that the non-empty instructions sum to 100 and attempts to create the ExpenseAllocation records.
A staff member or viewer reads the expense and derived totals.
outcomes: Under M26/M29, intake succeeds and stores allocations of -10 and 110; the section actual is -10 and other expenses total is 110.
Under the Modeling conventions, intake rejects the negative instruction because storing the -10 ExpenseAllocation would put a negative amount in a stored record.
witness.observer: The operator sees success versus rejection; subsequent staff and viewers see the expense and different derived totals only in the accepting implementation.
